title: Quinn Residence: an LRT link at the door, mountains at the back.
location: Sri Rampai, Wangsa Maju, Kuala Lumpur
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #482 | QUINN RESIDENCE, WANGSA MAJU
excerpt: A single block of 361 units linked to Sri Rampai LRT and Sunway Wangsa Mall, with a hill view behind. Sean loves the connectivity and rents, but finds the facilities impractical and the front noisy.
takeaways: Covered walkway to Sri Rampai LRT and a bridge to Sunway Wangsa Mall, near DUKE, MRR2 and the SPE.
Owners who paid about RM500,000 have rented two-bedroom units for about RM3,300 to RM3,800.
Front-facing units pick up highway and train noise, and some facilities are impractical in Malaysia's weather.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Quinn is a single block of 361 units on about 1.68 acres, designed with a foreign architect's eye for tall, compact spaces: steps, water features, a function hall that opens onto the children's pool, a rooftop co-working space and a small gym. Corridors are enclosed, with magnetic fire doors that stay open until an alarm.

Sean viewed a two-bedroom, two-bathroom Type B3 with an open kitchen and no yard or balcony, a ceiling of about 3 m and windows running the full width of the unit. The wall between the bedrooms can come down to make one large room.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: A covered walkway leads straight into Sri Rampai LRT station, and a bridge crosses to the refurbished Sunway Wangsa Mall, with more shops and eateries behind it. DUKE, MRR2, the new SPE highway and the Karak Highway are close, the planned ECRL station at Gombak is nearby, and colleges and the established Wangsa Maju community surround it, with Bukit Telekom rising behind the block.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: The owners who let Sean film bought for about RM500,000; similar units are now listed at about RM650,000 to RM680,000. Their unit has rented for about RM3,300 to RM3,800 a month. Construction was delayed through the movement control order, and Sean heard early buyers received six-figure compensation for late delivery.

standout.title: A wall you can take out
standout.body: In the two-bedroom unit, the short corridor to the master bedroom looks odd until the plans show the partition can be removed. Owners can keep two rooms or open them into one large, studio-like space that feels far more luxurious, for under RM600,000.

pros: The location: connected to KLCC by back roads, MRR2, DUKE and now the SPE, close to the ECRL and Karak Highway, with the LRT at the door and a mall across a bridge, yet with a mature community around it and a hill view from the back units.

The architecture: mature trees kept at the entrance, tall common spaces with landscaping and water, a function hall that opens onto the pool deck, well-lit lift lobbies, enclosed corridors that are safer and easier to maintain, and wide windows that stop short of floor and ceiling to reduce leaks. He also likes the extra-wide front door, the 1.45 m bathrooms and the removable bedroom wall.
The density: one block of only 361 units, which explains the compact facilities and means residents are likely to know each other.
cons: The foreign approach to space: tall pavilions with short canopies are unusable in rain or heat, the gym feels small, and the facility deck has many changes of level.
Noise: the SPE highway and the LRT echo loudly at the front. The back-facing unit he viewed was completely quiet, so orientation matters.
Competition: about ten projects stand within close range, from Quartz and Arvella to Artessa and Sfera, which is why Quinn's low density stands out.

closing: A rare mix of transit, mall and nature close to the city, good for own stay or investment; Sean says he regrets not buying one.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this November 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. Owners let Sean view their unit after completion; the purchase price and rents are theirs, and listing prices are as he quoted them.
